A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evidence from behavioral genetics suggests that education policy makers should be wary of assuming that the effects of educational interventions will be uniform across all students.
the genetic evidence suggests that educational achievement and attainment is highly influenced by genetic variation, and that genetic influences on educational outcomes are largely non-shared.

genetic evidence suggests that the effects of educational interventions are likely to be more modest than is often assumed, and that educational interventions may be more likely to be effective when they are tailored to the specific characteristics of the individuals or groups being served.

genetic evidence can help researchers and policy makers to understand how the environment affects people, and vice versa, and to understand the role of genetic differences in explaining the variation in outcomes.
